name: Logarithm rules
formula: \log_b (xy) = \log_b x + \log_b y, \quad \log_b \frac{x}{y} = \log_b x - \log_b y, \quad \log_b x^k = k \log_b x \quad (b > 0,\ b \ne 1,\ x, y > 0)
whenToUse: Simplify a sum or difference of logs with the same base, bring an exponent down, or turn an exponential equation into a linear one.
pitfall: There is no rule for $\log(x + y)$, and $\log_b x \cdot \log_b y$ is not $\log_b(xy)$. Logs are only defined for positive inputs, so check answers against that.
derivation: Logs are exponents: if $x = b^p$ and $y = b^q$ then $xy = b^{p+q}$, $\frac{x}{y} = b^{p-q}$ and $x^k = b^{kp}$.
